# Parse cutoff to a comparable datetime and fetch all pages until we have all requests
from datetime import datetime

# Convert cutoff to a string for comparison? Better to parse created_at to datetime.
# We'll fetch all pages until we get an empty list or all items are older than cutoff.
all_requests = []
page_index = 0
while True:
    current_page = venmo.show_received_payment_requests(access_token, page_index=page_index, page_limit=20)
    if not current_page:
        break
    all_requests.extend(current_page)
    # Check if all items in this page are older than cutoff (i.e., created_at < cutoff)
    # If so, we can stop because subsequent pages will be even older (assuming sorted by created_at descending)
    # But we don't know the sort order. Safer to continue until empty.
    # However, to avoid infinite loop, we can stop if the last item's created_at is before cutoff.
    # Let's check the last item's created_at.
    last_created = datetime.fromisoformat(current_page[-1]['created_at'])
    if last_created < cutoff:
        break
    page_index += 1

# Now filter requests within the last 7 days
recent_requests = [req for req in all_requests if datetime.fromisoformat(req['created_at']) >= cutoff]
print(f"Number of recent requests: {len(recent_requests)}")
print(recent_requests)
